senses.def: to tell someone about something officially or formally
examples: Passengers will be notified by text message if the flight is delayed.
You must notify the bank immediately if your card is stolen.

note: Pattern: notify someone OF something (not "notify something to someone" in everyday use). More formal than tell.

senses.def: an idea or belief about something, often one that is vague or not fully accepted
examples: She rejected the notion that women are less ambitious than men.
I had no notion of how expensive the repairs would be.

senses.tr: kötü şöhretli, adı çıkmış, dillere düşmüş
senses.def: famous for something bad
examples: The intersection is notorious for traffic accidents.
He was a notorious gang leader in the 1990s.

note: Always negative, unlike famous. Trap: Turkish "meşhur" can be neutral, but notorious is never a compliment.

senses.def: despite something; without being affected by it
examples: Notwithstanding the bad weather, the festival drew a huge crowd.
The project went ahead, budget problems notwithstanding.

senses.def: in spite of what has just been said
examples: The plan has some flaws; notwithstanding, we should give it a try.

note: Very formal, typical of legal and academic writing. It can come before or after the noun.

senses.def: a long written story about imaginary people and events, filling a whole book
examples: She spent three years writing her first novel.
I read a crime novel on the flight home.

senses.def: new and different from anything seen or done before
examples: Researchers have found a novel way to recycle plastic bottles.
The virus was a novel strain that doctors had never seen.

note: Trap: a novel is fiction. A non-fiction book is not a novel.

senses.def: a person who writes novels
examples: The novelist based the story on her childhood in Ohio.
He is best known as a novelist, but he also writes poetry.

senses.def: the eleventh month of the year, after October and before December
examples: Americans celebrate Thanksgiving in late November.
The election will be held on November 5.

note: Months always start with a capital letter in English. Use "in November" but "on November 5".

senses.def: at the present time
examples: I'm busy right now, can I call you back?
She now lives in Chicago with her husband.

senses.def: immediately
examples: If we leave now, we can still catch the train.

senses.def: because something has happened or is now true
examples: Now that the kids are in college, the house feels very quiet.

note: "Now that" means "because now". "For now" means "for the time being" (şimdilik).

senses.def: at the present time, compared with the past
examples: Nowadays most people pay with their phones instead of cash.
Kids nowadays spend hours a day on screens.

note: Used to contrast the present with the past. Do not use it for a single moment: say "now", not "nowadays I'm busy".

senses.def: not in any place or to any place
examples: The keys were nowhere to be found.
We had nowhere to stay, so we slept in the car.

senses.def: used to say that there is no progress or success
examples: The negotiations are going nowhere.

note: "Out of nowhere" = suddenly. "Nowhere near" = not at all, far from ("nowhere near enough").

senses.def: using or connected with the energy released when atoms are split or joined
examples: The country gets about a fifth of its electricity from nuclear power.
World leaders met to discuss reducing nuclear weapons.

senses.def: connected with the nucleus of a cell or an atom
examples: The study looked at changes in nuclear DNA.

note: "Nuclear family" = parents and their children only (çekirdek aile).

senses.def: a word or symbol that shows an amount, or a set of digits used to identify something
examples: Can I have your phone number?
Pick a number between one and ten.

senses.def: an amount or quantity of people or things
examples: A large number of students failed the test.
The number of cyclists in the city has doubled.

senses.def: to give each thing in a series a number
examples: Please number the pages before you print the report.

note: "A number of" takes a plural verb (A number of people are...), but "the number of" takes a singular verb (The number is...).

senses.def: existing in large numbers; many
examples: The senator has appeared on numerous TV shows.
We tried numerous times to contact the landlord.

note: More formal than many. Use it with plural countable nouns only.

senses.def: a person trained to care for sick or injured people, usually in a hospital
examples: The nurse checked my blood pressure before the doctor came in.
She has worked as a nurse in the emergency room for ten years.

senses.def: to care for someone who is sick or injured
examples: He nursed his wife through a long illness.

senses.def: a place where young children are looked after while their parents are at work
examples: She drops her son off at the nursery before work.
The company runs a nursery for employees' children.

senses.def: a place where young plants and trees are grown for sale
examples: We bought two apple trees at the local plant nursery.

senses.def: a room in a house where a baby sleeps
examples: They painted the nursery yellow before the baby arrived.

note: In American English, daycare or preschool is more common than nursery for childcare. "Nursery rhyme" = çocuk tekerlemesi.

senses.def: the job or skill of caring for sick or injured people
examples: She is studying nursing at a state university.
There is a shortage of nursing staff in rural hospitals.

note: "Nursing home" = a place where old people live and get care (huzurevi, bakımevi).

senses.def: a dry fruit with a hard shell that grows on some trees
examples: He snacks on nuts and fruit instead of chips.
This cake may contain nuts, so be careful if you're allergic.

senses.def: a small metal piece with a hole in it that screws onto a bolt
examples: Tighten the nuts on the wheel before you drive.

senses.def: a person who is very enthusiastic about something, or who is a little crazy
examples: My uncle is a real fitness nut who runs every morning.

note: Informal: "go nuts" = get very excited or angry; "the nuts and bolts" = the basic practical details.

senses.def: the process of getting the food needed for health and growth, or the study of this
examples: Good nutrition is essential for children's development.
Check the nutrition label for sugar and salt.

note: Nutritious food is healthy food; nutritional describes things related to nutrition (nutritional value).

senses.def: used after the numbers one to twelve to say an exact hour
examples: The meeting starts at ten o'clock sharp.
I woke up at six o'clock this morning.

note: Only for exact hours: say "three o'clock" but not "three thirty o'clock" or "15 o'clock".

senses.def: the condition of being so overweight that it is dangerous to health
examples: Childhood obesity has risen sharply over the past thirty years.
Obesity increases the risk of heart disease and diabetes.

senses.def: to do what a person, law or rule tells you to do
examples: Soldiers are trained to obey orders without question.
Drivers must obey the speed limit near schools.

note: Transitive: obey the law, not "obey to the law" (a common trap from Turkish "-e uymak").

senses.def: a thing that you can see and touch but that is not alive
examples: The museum displays everyday objects from ancient Rome.
Police found a sharp object in his bag.

senses.def: the purpose or aim of an activity
examples: The object of the game is to collect as many points as possible.

senses.def: to say that you disagree with or do not like something
examples: Many residents objected to the new parking rules.
I object to being treated like a child.

note: Stress shift: noun OBject /ˈɑːbdʒɪkt/, verb obJECT /əbˈdʒekt/. Verb pattern: object to + noun/-ing.

senses.def: a reason why you disagree with or oppose something, or a statement of this
examples: Does anyone have any objection to moving the meeting to Friday?
The plan went ahead despite strong objections from local residents.

senses.def: something you are trying to achieve
examples: Our main objective this year is to reduce costs.
The course has clear learning objectives.

senses.def: based on facts rather than personal feelings or opinions
examples: It's hard to be objective when your own child is involved.
We need objective evidence, not just opinions.

note: Opposite of the adjective: subjective.

senses.def: something you must do because of a law, a promise or a duty
examples: Employers have a legal obligation to provide a safe workplace.
You are under no obligation to buy anything.

note: "No obligation" in ads means you don't have to buy or commit ("a free, no-obligation quote").

senses.def: to force someone to do something because of a law, rule or duty
examples: The law obliges companies to publish their annual accounts.
I felt obliged to invite her, since she had invited me.

senses.def: to help someone by doing what they ask
examples: When the reporters asked for a photo, the singer happily obliged.

note: Usually passive: be/feel obliged to do something. "Much obliged" is an old-fashioned way to say thank you.

senses.def: the act of watching something carefully over time to learn about it
examples: The patient was kept in the hospital overnight for observation.
Her findings are based on years of careful observation.

senses.def: a comment based on something you have noticed
examples: He made an interesting observation about the way people use their phones.

senses.def: to see or notice something, or to watch it carefully
examples: Scientists observed the birds' behavior for six months.
Witnesses observed a man leaving the building at midnight.

senses.def: to obey a rule or law, or to follow a custom
examples: All visitors must observe the safety regulations.
Many families observe the holiday with a special meal.

senses.def: to make a remark about something you have noticed
examples: "It's getting late," she observed.

senses.def: a person who watches or notices something, or whose job is to watch an event and report on it
examples: International observers said the election was free and fair.
To a casual observer, the two paintings look identical.

senses.def: to fill someone's mind completely, or to think and worry about something all the time
examples: Stop obsessing about your weight; you look great.
She is obsessed with true crime podcasts.

note: Most common as "be obsessed with". Active use: obsess about/over something.

senses.def: a state in which one thing or person fills your mind all the time, in a way that is not normal
examples: His obsession with video games was hurting his grades.
Cleanliness has become an obsession for her.

senses.def: something that blocks your way or makes it hard to achieve something
examples: Lack of money is the biggest obstacle to starting a business.
The runners had to jump over several obstacles.

note: Pattern: an obstacle TO something (an obstacle to peace).

senses.def: to get something, especially through effort or an official process
examples: You need to obtain a visa before you travel.
The journalist obtained a copy of the secret report.

note: Formal. In everyday speech, people usually say get.

senses.def: easy to see, notice or understand
examples: It was obvious that she had been crying.
For obvious reasons, we can't discuss the case in public.

note: "State the obvious" = say something everyone already knows.

senses.def: used to say that something is easy to see or understand, or that people should already know it
examples: Obviously, we can't afford a new car right now.
He was obviously upset when he heard the news.

senses.def: a particular time when something happens
examples: I've met him on several occasions.
On one occasion, the train was three hours late.

senses.def: a special event or celebration
examples: She saves her best dress for special occasions.
The wedding was a joyful occasion for the whole family.

note: Spelling: two c's, one s. "Rise to the occasion" = deal successfully with a difficult situation.

senses.def: happening sometimes, but not often or regularly
examples: I don't smoke, apart from the occasional cigar at weddings.
The forecast is for sun with occasional showers.

senses.tr: ara sıra, arada bir, zaman zaman
senses.def: sometimes, but not often
examples: We occasionally eat out, but usually we cook at home.
Occasionally, the system crashes and we lose our work.

senses.def: a job or profession
examples: Please write your name, age and occupation on the form.
Nursing is one of the fastest-growing occupations.

senses.def: the act of an army taking control of a country or area
examples: The city was under military occupation for five years.

note: "Occupation" is formal and used on forms; in conversation, ask "What do you do?"

senses.def: to fill or use a space, area or period of time
examples: The bookshelves occupy an entire wall of the living room.
Is this seat occupied?

senses.def: to keep someone busy
examples: I brought some games to keep the kids occupied on the trip.

senses.def: to take control of a place by military force or as a protest
examples: Protesters occupied the university building for three days.

senses.def: to happen, especially without being planned
examples: The accident occurred on the highway just after midnight.
Most of these errors occur when users are tired.

senses.def: to come into your mind
examples: It never occurred to me that he might be lying.

senses.def: to exist or be found somewhere
examples: This mineral occurs naturally in volcanic rock.

note: Doubles the r: occurred, occurring, occurrence. "It occurred to me" = I suddenly thought of it.

senses.def: something that happens
examples: Power cuts are a common occurrence in this part of the city.
Car thefts are a rare occurrence in our neighborhood.

senses.def: the fact of something happening or existing, or how often it does
examples: Doctors are studying the occurrence of the disease in young adults.

note: Spelling: double c, double r: occurrence.

senses.def: the mass of salt water that covers most of the earth, or one of its large areas
examples: They rented a house with a view of the Pacific Ocean.
Plastic waste is a growing threat to ocean life.

note: Americans often say "the ocean" where British people say "the sea" (go swimming in the ocean).

senses.def: the tenth month of the year, after September and before November
examples: Halloween is celebrated on October 31.
The leaves start changing color in early October.

note: Months always start with a capital letter in English.

senses.def: strange or unusual
examples: It's odd that she hasn't called; she usually calls every day.
There was an odd smell coming from the fridge.

senses.def: (of a number) that cannot be divided exactly by two
examples: 1, 3, 5 and 7 are odd numbers.

senses.tr: ara sıra olan, çeşitli; teki kayıp
senses.def: happening sometimes but not regularly, or not part of a matching pair
examples: He does odd jobs around the neighborhood for extra money.
I have a drawer full of odd socks.

note: "The odd one out" = the one that is different from the rest. Opposite of odd number: even number.

senses.def: how likely it is that something will happen
examples: The odds of winning the lottery are about one in 300 million.
The odds are that prices will keep rising.

senses.def: difficulties that make success seem unlikely
examples: Against all odds, the small team won the championship.

note: Always plural. "Be at odds with" = disagree or not match (görüş ayrılığı içinde olmak).

senses.def: belonging to or connected with someone or something
examples: The roof of the house was damaged in the storm.
She is a friend of my sister.

senses.def: used to show an amount, a part or what something contains
examples: Could I have a glass of water, please?
Some of the students missed the bus.

senses.def: about or concerning
examples: Have you heard of this band?
I'm afraid of spiders.

note: In fast speech it often sounds like /ə/ ("kinda", "lotta"). Never write "could of"; the correct form is "could have".

senses.def: removed or separated, or no longer working or switched on
examples: Please turn off the lights when you leave.
Take your shoes off before you come in.

senses.def: away from a place, or not at work
examples: I'm off tomorrow, so let's meet for lunch.
She waved and drove off.

senses.def: down from or away from a surface or place
examples: The cat knocked the glass off the table.
Keep off the grass.

note: Trap: don't say "off of" in formal writing; "off the table" is enough. Also "20% off" = indirimli.

senses.def: to upset or insult someone by being rude or thoughtless
examples: I didn't mean to offend you; it was only a joke.
Many viewers were offended by the ad.

senses.def: to commit a crime
examples: Young people who offend are often victims themselves.

senses.def: a person who has committed a crime
examples: The program helps young offenders find jobs after prison.
First-time offenders usually receive a lighter sentence.

senses.def: a person or thing that does something wrong or causes a problem
examples: When it comes to air pollution, coal plants are the worst offenders.
